source_text:
ΠΕΡΙ ΤΗΣ ΕΝ ΠΝΕΥΜΑΤΙ ΚΑΙ ΑΛΗΘΕΙΑ ΠΡΟΣΚΥΝΗΣΕΩΣ ΚΑΙ ΛΑΤΡΕΙΑΣ ΛΟΓΟΣ ΕΠΤΑΚΑΙΔΕΚΑΤΟΣ. Περὶ ἑορτῶν ἁγίων. Ἁγνείας μὲν δὴ πέρι, καὶ τῶν ἐν εὐχαῖς, καὶ μέντοι καὶ ἱερέων εἰρήσθω τάδε. Χρῆναι δὲ οἶμαι λοιπὸν προσενεγκεῖν εὖ μάλα, τίς ἂν γένοιτο παρὰ Θεοῦ τῶν πόνων ἔκτισις, καὶ πρὸς ὅ τι τετραμμένοι, καταπιανθεῖεν ἂν ταῖς εἰς λῆξιν ἡκούσαις τιμαῖς, καὶ ἐλπίδος ἔσονται τῆς εἰς αἰῶνας μέτοχοι.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὡς εὖ γε δὴ φής.
{ΚΥΡ.} Πρέποι γὰρ ἂν, ὦ Παλλάδιε, τοῖς τὴν εὐκλεᾶ καὶ ἀπόλεκτον ἐξησκηκόσι ζωὴν, καὶ πολιτείας τῆς ὧδε διαφανοῦς εἰς τοῦτο ἥκουσι μέτρον, ὡς τὴν ἁπασῶν ἀρίστην ψῆφον ἑλεῖν, ἐν εὐημερίαις εἶναι μακραῖς, ἑορτάζοντάς τε καὶ διευθυμουμένους, καὶ πανηγύρεως ἀρχὴν ἔχοντας τὸν Ἐμμανουὴλ, καὶ ἐν ἐλπίσι κειμένους ταῖς ἐρηρεισμέναις.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Πρέποι γὰρ ἂν, καὶ ἀληθὴς ὁ λόγος.
{ΚΥΡ.} Βούλει δὴ οὖν, τὰς ἐν τύπῳ καὶ κατὰ νόμον πολυπραγμονῶμεν ἑορτὰς καὶ τῶν ἐν αὐταῖς θυσιῶν τοὺς τρόπους ἀφηγησώμεθα, μεταστοιχειοῦντες, ὡς ἔνι, πρὸς τὸ ἀληθὲς τῶν ἐν αὐταῖς ἐννοιῶν τὴν δύναμιν;
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Βουλοίμην ἄν· πῶς γὰρ οὔ;
{ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν ἐπεί τοι σαφῶς ἄριστά τε διεσκέφθαι δοκῶ, φιλοκρινεῖν ὅτι πρέποι καὶ τάδε διενθυμούμενος, φέρε δὴ, φέρε καὶ πρό γε τῶν ἄλλων ἐκεῖνο διερευνήσωμεν, πηνίκα τε καὶ ἐπὶ τίσιν ἑορτάζειν ἡμᾶς τὸ Γράμμα δεῖν ἔφη τὸ ἱερόν. Ἴοι γὰρ ἂν οὕτω καὶ κατ' εὐθὺ τοῦ πρέποντος ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος· καὶ μέντοι πρὸς τῷδε, τὸ ἀτέχνως πεποιῆσθαι δοκεῖν οὐκ ἀγεννῶς διακρούσεται.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the worship and service in spirit and truth, seventeenth discourse. Concerning holy feasts. About purity, then, and about the things in prayers, and indeed also about priests, let these things have been said. And I think it is needful next to bring forward very well what repayment of the labors would come from God, and turned toward what they would be fattened with the honors that have come to the final allotment, and will be partakers of the hope for the ages. PALL.: How well you say it. CYR.: For it would befit, O Palladius, those who have practiced the renowned and select life, and have come to this measure of the conduct conspicuous here, so as to take the best vote of all, to be in long good days, feasting and rejoicing greatly, and having Emmanuel as beginning of festival, and lying in the firmly fixed hopes. PALL.: For it would befit, and true is the word. CYR.: Do you wish then that we busy ourselves about the feasts in type and according to law and narrate the manners of the sacrifices in them, transforming, as is possible, toward the true the force of the thoughts in them? PALL.: I would wish it; for how not? CYR.: Therefore, since I seem to have considered clearly and very well that it would befit to judge carefully, pondering these things too, come then, come, and before the others let us search out that: at what time and on what (occasions) the sacred Letter said we must feast. For thus the account would go straight toward what befits us; and besides this, it will not ignobly ward off the seeming to have been made artlessly.
pass_b_english: ON ADORATION AND WORSHIP IN SPIRIT AND TRUTH — BOOK SEVENTEEN. On the holy feasts.

Cyril: Let this much be said about purity, about prayers, and indeed about priests. Next, I think, we ought to set out with great care what repayment for their labors would come from God, and by turning toward what they would be enriched with the honors that come at the final allotment, and become sharers in the hope that lasts for ages.
Palladius: How well you put it.

Cyril: For it would be fitting, Palladius, that those who have practiced the glorious and chosen life, and have come so far in conduct, shining here below, that they carry off the best verdict of all, should live in long days of gladness, keeping feast and rejoicing, with Emmanuel as the beginning of their festival, and resting on firmly grounded hopes.
Palladius: It would indeed be fitting, and what you say is true.

Cyril: Shall we, then, look closely into the feasts kept in type and according to the law, and describe the manner of the sacrifices offered at them, carrying over, as far as we can, the force of their meanings into the truth?
Palladius: I would like that; how could I not?

Cyril: Well then, since I think I have reasoned it out clearly and well that, as we ponder these things too, we ought to judge them with care, come, come, let us first of all search out when, and on what occasions, the sacred Writing said that we must keep feast. For in this way our discussion would go straight along the fitting road; and besides, it will nobly ward off any appearance of having been put together without art.

choices.english: the honors that come at the final allotment
choices.why: λῆξις is the allotted portion at the end; the old English 'honors that reach their fulfillment' blurred it.

choices.term: ἐπεί τοι σαφῶς ἄριστά τε διεσκέφθαι δοκῶ, φιλοκρινεῖν ὅτι πρέποι
choices.english: since I think I have reasoned it out clearly and well that ... we ought to judge them with care
choices.why: Kept the hard construction as one sentence; the old English turned it into 'these are excellent things'.
Cyril's name for the law here; kept distinct from 'Scripture'.
